fact: BCEAO launched PI-SPI on 30 September 2025, letting anyone with an account at a bank, microfinance institution or e-money or payment institution connected to it send and receive money instantly across WAEMU, whatever the provider.
The article says Mobile Money has become the standard for transactions and that the Xedo platform integrates Mobile Money settlement for Beninese merchants.
Transfers from banks can credit mobile money wallets in seconds and the reverse, in real time, via PI-SPI, which the article says now connects banks and mobile money 100% in UEMOA.
Arcep reports 11,649,735 active mobile financial services accounts at 31 December 2025, led by MTN Mobile Money (51%), Celtiis Cash (27%) and Moov Money (22%).
BCEAO reports 80 participants connected to PI-SPI on 2 April 2026: 59 banks, 9 e-money institutions, 11 microfinance institutions and 1 payment institution, on one interoperable platform.
Benin had 37.5 million e-money accounts, 11.2 million active, at the end of 2024, per the BCEAO report.
Benin recorded 2.09 billion electronic money transactions in 2023, 22.22% of the UEMOA total, per a BCEAO report cited by Fraternite.
Banks and mobile operators offer PUSH & PULL transfers between bank accounts and mobile money wallets, per Fraternite.
Fraternité reported mobile money agents serving Moov Money and MTN MoMo customers in Cotonou, with deposits and withdrawals in service.
Fraternité reports Mobile Money is the most widespread e-money service in Benin, offered by three providers: MTN Mobile Money, Moov Money and Celtiis Cash.
